evidence.quote: As-cast Ti45V45Cr5Al5 MPEA ingot was prepared by arc-melting the mixtures of Ti, V, Cr, and Al (purities > 99.9 wt%) under a high-purity argon atmosphere. The ingot was melted at least six times to ensure compositional homogeneity, and elliptical ingots with dimensions of 70 mm × 40 mm × 12 mm were obtained.
Finally, the ingots were cold-rolled into a sheet with 87 % thickness reduction (denoted as CR).
The cold-rolled samples were annealed at 700 ℃, 800 ℃, and 1000 ℃ for 1 h under vacuum atmosphere, followed by water quenching (referred as CR-700, CR-800, and CR-1000 for convenience).

evidence.quote: a new diffraction peak corresponding to the FCC-Ti phase appeared in the CR-800 sample, which represents an uncommon Ti crystal structure
TEM analysis revealed that the nucleation sites for the Ti-rich nanoprecipitates are located at the grain boundaries of the BCC matrix.
It is evident that the as-cast MPEA exhibits relatively large grain sizes, with an average diameter of 379 μm.
with the average grain diameter of the CR-700 sample being only 3 μm
As the annealing temperature increases, the grain size increases, reaching 6 μm in the CR-800 sample.
Severe rolling deformation elongated and fragmented grains along the rolling direction (RD). Intense deformation generated numerous deformation microbands (black regions in Fig. 3 b).
